name: Snappa
tagline: Compose fixed-size social graphics from local images, text, and a small template set

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: 1 user, 3 downloads/month, 6,000+ templates and 5 million+ stock assets.

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: Up to 5 users, unlimited downloads and team collaboration.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1 user and 3 downloads per month; 6,000+ templates and 5 million+ stock assets.
pricing.hiddenCosts: Teams larger than 5 users require contacting Snappa for pricing.

verdictSummary: The core loop is small enough for a capable coding agent to produce a useful local version in one sitting. For Snappa, compose fixed-size social graphics from local images, text, and a small template set. The hard boundary is stock-photo allowance, templates, team sharing, and cloud convenience, plus editor polish, assets, collaboration, and distribution.
coreLoopDIY: Compose fixed-size social graphics on a canvas from local images, text, and a small set of reusable templates, then export a polished SVG or PDF.
whatYouLose: stock-photo allowance, templates, team sharing, and cloud convenience
moatNotes: editor polish, assets, collaboration, and distribution
ongoingBurden: canvas correctness, fonts, exports, templates, asset rights, multiplayer state, and accessibility
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Snappa because people pay for a vast ready-made design system and a collaboration surface that behaves predictably under deadline. The recurring cost buys canvas correctness, fonts, exports, templates, asset rights, multiplayer state, and accessibility, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Penpot
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source collaborative design platform with SVG-native editing.

alternatives.name: Adobe Express Free
alternatives.desc: Quick social graphics from templates, stock, text, and local images, with a real free export path.

facts.install: Hosted signup in a browser, or install the Adobe Express desktop/mobile app.
facts.engines: Adobe Firefly models power the generative features.
facts.dataFormat: Projects, uploads, libraries and brand assets live in Adobe's cloud; exports include image, PDF and video files.
facts.gapVsPaid: Adobe Express's broader interface is slower and more complex than Snappa's intentionally narrow fixed-size social-graphic workflow.

alternatives.name: Canva Free
alternatives.desc: Fixed-size social templates, local uploads, text, and unlimited ordinary exports; vastly larger than the small tool it replaces.

facts.install: Hosted signup in a browser, or install Canva's desktop/mobile app.
facts.engines: Canva AI and Magic Studio provide generative tools; Canva does not publish a complete provider/model map for the free editor.
facts.dataFormat: Designs, uploads, folders and brand assets live in Canva's cloud; users export common image, PDF, presentation and video formats.
facts.gapVsPaid: Canva is vastly more capable but also more cluttered than Snappa's fast, small-tool workflow.

alternatives.name: Desygner Free
alternatives.desc: Straightforward social graphics, templates, photo tools, and scheduling for three users without download rationing.

facts.install: Hosted signup in a browser, or install the mobile app.
facts.engines: Desygner's terms identify OpenAI-backed AI features.
facts.dataFormat: Projects, uploads, fonts and brand assets live in Desygner's cloud; designs export as image or PDF files.
facts.gapVsPaid: Desygner is less polished and immediate than Snappa for rapidly assembling a fixed-size graphic.

alternatives.name: VistaCreate Starter
alternatives.desc: A generous free social-template editor with one brand kit, stock assets, animation, and unlimited downloads.

facts.install: Hosted signup in a browser, or install the mobile app.
facts.dataFormat: Projects, uploads and the single Brand Kit live in VistaCreate's cloud; exports include image, GIF and video files.
facts.gapVsPaid: VistaCreate's larger animation and template surface makes it less direct than Snappa for a simple static social image.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Snappa Starter
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Free forever, technically; three downloads per month is a sample counter, not a usable social-graphics workflow.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a personal design canvas DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Snappa in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, React, Tailwind CSS, IndexedDB, and SVG; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: compose fixed-size social graphics on a canvas from local images, text, and a small set of reusable templates, then export a polished SVG or PDF.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create a fixed-size SVG canvas with zoom, pan, selection, alignment, and snapping.
Support text, rectangles, circles, images, groups, layers, and reusable components.
Add a small set of high-quality starter layouts relevant to the product category.
Implement undo, redo, autosave, and import or export of a portable project JSON file.
Export SVG and print-ready PDF without rasterizing text unnecessarily.
Keep all assets local and display missing-font warnings before export.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out real-time multiplayer editing.
Deliberately leave out a commercial stock-asset library.
Deliberately leave out enterprise brand controls and approval workflows.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
